recipes.name: Chicken Salad with Bacon, Lettuce, and Tomato
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Cook bacon in a large skillet and over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned and crispy, about 10 minutes. Drain on paper towels and crumble when cool enough to handle.
Whisk mayonnaise, green onion, parsley, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and black pepper together in a bowl until smooth.
Stir chicken, tomato, and celery together in a bowl. Add crumbled bacon; pour mayonnaise dressing over top and toss to coat. Cover and refrigerate until chilled, at least 30 minutes.
When ready to serve, remove from the refrigerator and stir. Serve over romaine lettuce leaves and garnish with avocado slices.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Salad with Bacon, Lettuce, and Tomato
raw_recipe.description: This chicken salad with bacon and tomato is dressed in a creamy mixture of mayonnaise, lemon juice, and parsley and served over crisp lettuce leaves.

video.description: What better way to jazz up chicken salad then by adding the delicious flavors of a BLT sandwich! Crisp bacon, fresh tomatoes and a creamy dressing full of fresh herbs makes it the perfect complement to a chicken salad. Serve it over leaves of fresh lettuce with avocado slices and your lunch will be the talk of the town.

review.reviewBody: Delicious! I love chicken salads and anything with bacon is bound to be good so I had to give this a try. I used leftover rotisserie chicken and 1/2 cup of Hellman's light mayo with 1/4 cup of light sour cream for the dressing. I de-seeded my tomato so nothing would get "watery". I loved the crunch from the celery and instead of just placing this on a plate as a "salad", I decided to roll this up inside large tortillas with the romaine lettuce and avocado slices because afterall, some chicken salads deserve to be eaten with your hands rather than just a fork!

Skipped the tomato, added leftover green peppers and cucumbers. Also added olive oil and extra lemon juice because the mixture was thick. I had a very ripe avocado, so I mixed it into the dressing. Delicious!

I just put this together for dinner tonight. Wow! I made the dressing with light mayo and dried parsley. I used the packaged grilled chicken breast strips from Costco and increased the bacon to eight slices. I mixed the celery with the chicken, tomatoes, and bacon, then tossed in the dressing. When I licked the spoon...WOW!! I will serve it with shredded butter leaf lettuce tonight. I've been looking for a go-to chicken salad recipe and I think I found it! Easy to make with staple ingredients. Yummy!!

This chicken salad is delicious!! I make it often and everybody loves it. I made just a few small changes: I used 1 tsp. dried parsley and 1 tablespoon chopped green onion instead of 2 (I'm not a huge fan of strong onion flavor). I cooked my chicken in the oven at 350 for 20 minutes. I used 3 boneless breasts (trimmed and tenderized just a little with a meat mallet) and drizzled with olive oil, seasoned with salt & pepper. it turns out firm but tender. I like chunks in my chicken salad.

Of course I couldn't follow the recipe. Is that even allowed? No romaine in the house. I was really looking for a recipe that I could use up the chicken I had thawed for last night and not cooked. Since we were going for a bike ride, it had to be picnic-able, so I went for a chicken salad. I marinaded my chicken breasts for 45 minutes or so in lemon juice with a dash of Worcestershire, then grilled and diced them.I burned the bacon because I was trying to do too many things at once, but it didn't hurt anything. I did have parsley, green onions, and tomato, so I used them along with some red cabbage that clamored to be included. No mayo, so the dressing became a dash of brown mustard, a couple dollops of miracle whip, some Ken's Vidalia Onion dressing, and some Beets All Ranch dressing. Added some grated parmesan just because parmesan. At the picnic table we wrapped them in tortillas and devoured them. Thanks for the inspiration and guidance! My wife insisted that I add this to my favorites.

This was an absolute hit in my house! IMHO I almost never follow recipes exactly as written; it’s more of a template. So when making this I probably used more chicken and celery than required and I definitely added more citrus to the sauce. Really though what made this for my house was adding cilantro rather than just parsley. I feel bad for those who taste soap rather than the AWESOMENESS that is cilantro!

Made this as written and it was outstanding! Tasted just like a great BLT sandwich. The only thing I found was it was a little thick, so added a bit more lemon juice to thin it out a bit. I also skipped the avocado as this is something I'm not that big a fan of.

If you want to make this a touch healthier, substitute Plain Greek Yogurt for the mayo. I just made a batch of the dressing with yogurt, juice of half a lemon and 1% milk to get the consistency right and it is superb! In a carton in my fridge for lunch salads and a veggie dip!

Thanks for a great recipe!
I thought this was great. I added less mayo. I didn't add celery. I added some sliced sweet gherkin pickles, some pickle relish, a golden delicious apple, and crushed walnuts.

I have made this salad twice now this summer. Both were hits. I have to admit, I hate it when writers say how wonderful a recipe was only to say they made all these changes but here I go. I love the addition of bacon to the salad but I really like to add fruit to give a sweetness and a variety of textures. I added sliced green olives, sliced red grapes, pineapple and walnuts. The lemon and Worcestershire sauce gives a nice zing. My Bunco and Beach friends were very complimentary. Thanks Brit!
Always looking for new chicken salad recipes to try. This was very good. I used a little over 1/4 cup of mayo and found that to be plenty. Will be making this again.

This is a good base recipe to be adjusted depending on personal taste preferences. My suggestions: Unless you *love* celery, leave it out, definitely mix the chopped avocado in with the chicken, tomatoes and bacon. The dressing was a tad bland even after I added garlic powder and a splash of white balsamic vinegar. We ended up squeezing a little extra fresh lemon juice over the top of the salad (placed on a bed of mixed greens) and it did the trick. I would also use red onion instead of green onion. I sprinkled the top with a little crumbled blue cheese and slivered almonds, which I would repeat (perhaps walnuts instead).

Great recipe. I added lots of crunchy vegetables like bell peppers and radishes. Like some others, I used half mayo and half sour cream. Made for a great taste. To make it easy, I just halved grape tomatoes.
A perfect summer dish to make with barbecued chicken. It's a great combination of both flavors and textures. Don't skip the romaine! It's not the same dish without that dark leafy flavored crunch.

I halved the recipe, there's just 2 of us. I also added croutons right before serving. It is very tasty and does taste like a BLT. This will be made again, this time for the 6 servings and maybe some cheese. That was last night, I forgot to submit. I made it AGAIN for the 2nd night in a row. I added some cubed cheddar cheese and a little onion powder to the dressing.
Absolutely perfect! A great spring salad for Sunday afternoons.
Ok but not a favorite. Needs more seasoning and does not save well.
A weekly rotation in our house. Excellent for a quick lunch and my young kids love it (which is rare). I use rotisserie chicken to speed up the process. Delicious!

Made a couple of adjustments because of what I had on hand. I used 5 Tbsp real bacon bits, 3 cups diced rotisserie chicken, 1 cup minced green pepper (in place of celery), +/- ¾ cup mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons minced frozen onion, 1 tsp dried parsley, 1 teaspoon lemon juice, 1 dash Worcestershire sauce, and salt and ground black pepper to taste.
I sliced the tomato and topped sandwiches with it when serving, along with romaine lettuce. We ate it on mini croissants, and everyone loved it!!
Excellent

Really yummy! I like spicy stuff, so next time I make it I will probably spice the chicken up while it cooks. Totally love this dish though. Maybe I will also add more lemon juice on top of the whole salad. I lunch a bit more of a punch to things but this salad was super yummy. Two thumbs up!
